Kathmandu, Nepal – Rescuers recovered the bodies on Friday of two Japanese climbers missing for over a week on a remote Himalayan mountain, an expedition organizer said.

The climbers were attempting the first summit of the 7,140-meter (23,425-foot) Gangapurna West in alpine style, but lost contact after Oct. 15.

description: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Economic Digest presents a brief yet comprehensive roundup of major business developments in Nepal, delivered in clear and accessible summaries.

Recent developments in Nepal highlight the government’s efforts to strengthen regional diplomacy, expand financial access, improve public administration and address climate-related vulnerabilities. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle’s engagement with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other Indian leaders at the NDTV World Summit underscores the importance of Nepal–India relations, particularly in economic cooperation and regional stability.

International climate financing has also gained significance, with the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage agreeing to allocate USD 20 million for flood recovery. However, the requirement for a detailed project proposal highlights the need for effective planning and implementation. Similarly, UNFPA’s climate-resilient healthcare model in Rautahat demonstrates how targeted infrastructure investment and qualified health workers can protect essential services during disasters.

In the financial sector, collateral-free digital loans and the restoration of banking services reflect expanding digital access and the growing importance of cybersecurity. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court’s ruling on demonetized Indian banknotes clarifies the legal interpretation of foreign exchange offenses. The government’s concessional vehicle loan scheme for public officials, however, raises questions about fiscal priorities and equitable use of public resources.

Tourism recovery in Myagdi and Mustang indicates renewed economic activity following monsoon disruptions, while rising traffic congestion exposes infrastructure and mobility challenges. Overall, these developments underscore the need to balance economic growth, institutional accountability, disaster resilience and sustainable development through coordinated policies and effective implementation.

Finance Minister Wagle meets Indian PM Modi at NDTV World Summit

Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly in New Delhi on Thursday evening during the NDTV World Summit 2026, following a major address by the Indian leader. Wagle arrived in the Indian capital on Thursday as an invited international speaker and delivered a special session titled “Prosperity through Proximity: India–Nepal Opportunity” at Hotel Taj Palace. During the visit, he also took part in a session featuring Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. The discussions focused on the evolving global order, bilateral ties and opportunities for economic cooperation between Nepal and India.

FRLD allocates $20 million for flood recovery in Nepal

The Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has agreed to allocate USD 20 million (approximately Rs 3.26 billion) to assist recovery and reconstruction efforts in Nepal’s flood-hit areas. The decision follows Nepal’s appeal for emergency support after devastating floods struck the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river region on August 26, resulting in fatalities and widespread destruction. However, the allocation does not mean the funds have already been released. Nepal must first submit a detailed project proposal for review and approval before the money can be disbursed. The decision is an important step towards obtaining international assistance for climate-related disasters, although the amount covers only part of Nepal’s overall recovery and reconstruction requirements.

Eleven banks offer collateral-free phone loans of up to Rs 200,000

Eleven commercial banks in Nepal are offering collateral-free digital loans, known as Phone Loan, allowing eligible customers to borrow up to Rs 200,000 directly through mobile banking applications without submitting physical documents or pledging assets. The participating banks are Everest Bank, Nabil Bank, NIC Asia Bank, NMB Bank, Citizens Bank, Kumari Bank, Laxmi Sunrise Bank, Machhapuchhre Bank, Prabhu Bank, Rastriya Banijya Bank and Agriculture Development Bank. Borrowing limits are determined automatically by system algorithms that assess customers’ account transaction histories over the preceding six months. Although repayment periods generally span one year, some banks offer terms of up to two years, providing greater flexibility for salaried customers and regular depositors.

Supreme Court rules demonetized Indian notes cannot establish foreign exchange offenses

The Supreme Court has ruled that demonetized foreign banknotes that no longer hold legal tender status in their country of origin cannot serve as the legal basis for establishing offenses under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1962. The ruling overturned earlier court decisions in a case stemming from July 17, 2018, when authorities seized Rs 5.3 million worth of demonetized Indian banknotes from a hotel in Rupandehi. The apex court observed that once the issuing monetary authority withdraws a currency’s legal tender status, the notes lose their essential characteristics as money. Consequently, possession of invalidated banknotes does not, by itself, amount to an illegal foreign exchange transaction. The full text of the verdict was released on July 30, 2026.

Government introduces concessional vehicle loans of up to Rs 6 million for public officials

The government has introduced a concessional loan scheme for public employees to purchase official vehicles under the Government Employees Vehicle Management Guideline, 2026, with the government covering the full interest cost. Loan ceilings vary according to administrative rank, with chief secretaries and secretaries eligible for up to Rs 6 million, joint secretaries Rs 5 million, and under-secretaries Rs 4 million. Section officers can receive up to Rs 400,000 to purchase two-wheelers, while non-gazetted employees are eligible for up to Rs 200,000. Repayment periods may extend to 20 years. Officials who choose to drive their vehicles themselves instead of using assigned institutional drivers will also receive an additional cash allowance equivalent to the standard salary of a driver.

Traffic congestion rises at major entry points to Kathmandu Valley

Traffic congestion has intensified at major entry points to the Kathmandu Valley as people return home after the festive holidays. Authorities have reported increased vehicle movement along key routes, including Nagdhunga–Kalanki, Jadibuti–Koteshwor, Tinpipale, Jagati, Bhattedanda and Dakshinkali–Farping. Traffic police have been deployed to manage the flow of vehicles and reduce the risk of road accidents. Daily traffic at major checkpoints currently averages around 1,000 vehicles. Official records show that 79,676 vehicles carried 576,578 people out of the capital between Ghatasthapana and October 20 for the annual festivities. The continuing return of holiday travellers is expected to keep major highways and entry routes busy in the coming days.

Machhapuchhre Bank and Nabil Bank restore full digital banking services

Machhapuchhre Bank and Nabil Bank have announced the full restoration of their web-based platforms, mobile banking services and other digital banking facilities following temporary suspensions. The interruptions were linked to system upgrades undertaken in response to global software vulnerabilities and broader security assessments. Bank officials said technical reviews and security enhancements had been completed to protect customer information and financial transaction systems. With the maintenance work finished, previously unavailable services—including debit card requests, credit card applications and secured loan processing—are operational again for retail and corporate customers across Nepal.

Tourist arrivals pick up in Myagdi and Mustang after festive holidays

Tourism activity is recovering in Myagdi and nearby destinations following the festive holidays, helped by favorable weather and the reopening of the Beni–Jomsom highway after the monsoon season. Local businesses have reported a steady flow of visitors to popular attractions, including Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Khopara, Singa Tatopani, Bhurung–Tatopani, Annapurna Base Camp, Rupse and Galeshwar. Travel had been severely affected by heavy monsoon flooding along the Kaligandaki river corridor during the second-to-last week of September. However, road clearance work completed late last month has restored vehicle access to the affected areas. Poon Hill, situated at an altitude of 3,210 metres, and nearby trekking routes continue to draw domestic and international visitors. Around 150 domestic tourists have reportedly departed for base camp excursions.

More than 700 foreign tourists enter Mustang via Thorong La Pass after snow clearance

A total of 772 foreign tourists have entered Mustang over the past two weeks after crossing Thorong La Pass from Besisahar through Manang, following operations to clear snow from the route. Records maintained by the Annapurna Conservation Area Project checkpoint in Jomsom show that the arrivals included 43 visitors from South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) member countries and 729 from other nations. The pass, located at an altitude of 5,416 metres along the Annapurna Circuit trekking route, is exposed to severe seasonal weather conditions. Joint efforts by local tourism entrepreneurs and security personnel helped clear the snow and reopen the trail. Tourism representatives said more than 100 trekkers are crossing the pass daily towards Muktinath, with high-altitude trekking expected to continue until the end of November.

UNFPA introduces scalable model for climate-resilient healthcare in Rautahat

The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) has established a model for climate-resilient maternal and newborn healthcare in Nepal, demonstrating how frontline health facilities can maintain life-saving services during severe climate-related disasters. The model was highlighted during a policy dialogue and field visit to the Auraiya Birthing Centre in Ishnath Municipality, Madhesh Province. The event brought together government representatives, healthcare providers and community leaders to review successful adaptation measures and chart a roadmap for scaling up climate-resilient health infrastructure in other vulnerable regions of Nepal, according to a UNFPA press release issued today. During an official visit to the centre, United Nations Resident Coordinator in Nepal Lila Pieters Yahia said even small, targeted investments could significantly improve access to maternal healthcare. “My visit to Auraiya Birthing Centre showed me how even small, targeted investments can make a real difference in access to maternal healthcare. What struck me most was the importance of having a qualified nurse at the health post. Her presence has built trust in the community, giving rural women, including those in more conservative communities, the confidence to seek care during pregnancy and after childbirth,” she said.

KATHMANDU: Nepal is likely to experience changing weather conditions next week, with rain and snowfall forecast in parts of the country from October 28 to November 1

The Weather Forecasting Division has urged people to remain alert as a low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal could influence the weather.

According to the Division’s weather forecast bulletin issued on Saturday morning, weather conditions are expected to remain generally stable over the next three days. However, the possibility of rain and snowfall is expected to increase from Wednesday through Sunday.

The Division said a low-pressure area had developed over the east-central and adjoining southeastern Bay of Bengal, potentially influencing weather conditions in Nepal during the period.

The Division has urged the public to remain alert and take necessary precautions in view of the possibility of changing weather conditions.

Rain and snowfall could affect travel, trekking and other outdoor activities, particularly in mountainous and high-altitude areas. Travellers, trekkers, farmers and communities in potentially affected regions are advised to follow official weather updates and plan their activities accordingly.

full_article:
KATHMANDU: Former President Bidya Devi Bhandari has urged the international community to take Nepal’s call for climate justice seriously, saying recent devastating natural disasters have once again exposed the country’s vulnerability to climate change.

Addressing the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), organised by the China Institute of International Studies in China, Bhandari outlined Nepal’s priorities for achieving climate justice, according to her secretariat.

Linking global governance directly to climate justice, Bhandari described the Himalayas as a shared natural heritage that plays a vital role in regional water cycles, biodiversity and ecological balance.

She stressed the need for greater cooperation among Himalayan countries, including China, Nepal and India, in climate data sharing, glacier monitoring, early warning systems and disaster response to protect the region and mitigate the impacts of climate change.

Bhandari also called for stronger regional and international cooperation to reduce climate risks, alongside sustained and reliable support from the United Nations and international financial institutions.

“Nepal supports a world order in which international law, rather than power, guides relations, the voices of all nations are respected, and the concerns of vulnerable countries receive due consideration,” she said, emphasising the need to strengthen the United Nations as an effective institution that reflects the diversity and aspirations of the contemporary world.

Highlighting the close relationship between peace and development, the former president said the international community shares responsibility for eliminating poverty and hunger, improving human welfare and redirecting resources spent on the arms race towards development.

She further underscored the importance of making international cooperation more effective in promoting inclusive, resilient and environmentally sustainable development. Poverty reduction, quality education and healthcare, employment, social justice and environmental protection, she said, should be central priorities of global cooperation.

Bhandari also highlighted the longstanding ties between Nepal and China, shaped by cultural exchanges, Buddhist philosophy and close people-to-people relations.

Stating that no single country can independently address the complex challenges facing the world, she stressed the importance of dialogue, cooperation and collective commitment. She noted that the UN Charter, international law and a multilateral world order have made significant contributions to international peace, security and development.

Bhandari expressed confidence that the forum would generate new opportunities for cooperation in advancing global peace, sustainable development and shared prosperity through meaningful discussions aimed at making global governance more just, inclusive and effective.

title: Bay of Bengal cyclone could bring rain, snow to Nepal next week - The Kathmandu Post
description: Bay of Bengal cyclone could bring rain, snow to Nepal next week  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Clear skies following the end of Nepal’s monsoon could give way to unsettled weather next week as a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a cyclonic storm, potentially bringing rain to parts of Nepal and snowfall in the high Himalayas.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, in a special post-monsoon weather bulletin issued on Friday, warned that the system could affect Nepal from October 28 to November 1. Meteorologists have urged farmers to protect their ripening paddy crops and trekkers to exercise caution in high-altitude areas.

According to the department, a low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining southeastern Bay of Bengal at 5:45 am on Friday. The system is expected to strengthen, move west-northwestwards and develop into a cyclonic storm by Monday before moving towards the coast of northern Andhra Pradesh and adjoining southern Odisha in India.

The department said it was too early to determine the amount of rainfall Nepal could receive or the level of risk, but warned that the weather system could affect agriculture and tourism.

The India Meteorological Department said in a bulletin issued on Saturday that the system was strengthening. It forecast that the low-pressure area would intensify into a depression and then a deep depression on Sunday before developing into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.

The system is expected to strengthen further as it moves west-northwestwards, reaching the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast by Wednesday morning.

Meteorologist Binod Pokharel, who shared a weather analysis on social media, warned of potential weather-related risks across Nepal from October 29 to November 1. Current forecasts indicate rain across much of the country, with heavy downpours possible in some areas.

He said the risk of rainfall would be relatively high on October 30 and 31. The forecast points to possible weather-related risks in Kathmandu and 28 districts across Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces. Manang also warrants particular attention, he said.

Pokharel noted that the low-pressure system from the Bay of Bengal could interact with an upper-level trough, increasing the likelihood of heavy rainfall.

He urged farmers to monitor local forecasts and make arrangements to protect ripening paddy still standing in fields, as well as harvested crops laid out to dry, from potential damage.

Climate and environment expert Ujjwal Upadhyay also forecast rainfall across the country from October 28 to November 1. He urged farmers to harvest and bring in their crops and recommended suspending trekking in the high Himalayas during the period.

Upadhyay said the weather system could affect Nepal for nearly a week, although that did not necessarily mean continuous rainfall. There could be breaks in the rain, but the weather was unlikely to clear completely, with further showers possible at intervals, he said.

As the system continues to develop, rainfall could intensify, with hail also possible in some places, Upadhyay warned.

title: Nepali Congress falls short of one-third women’s quota in central committee - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepali Congress falls short of one-third women’s quota in central committee  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Women have secured 69 of the 231 elected positions on the Nepali Congress central committee, accounting for 29.87 percent of elected members. All won seats reserved for women or allocated under the party’s inclusion categories.

The party’s statute requires women to make up at least one-third of executive committees at every level. The 297-member central committee comprises 231 elected members and 66 nominees appointed by the party president. Three women were elected to office-bearing posts, while 66 won central committee seats.

With 69 women elected, party president Gagan Thapa must nominate at least 30 women to the 66 appointed seats to bring female representation to 99, or one-third of the committee.

Although the new committee includes representatives from a wider range of ethnic, social and professional groups, no woman won an unreserved seat.

The party reserved one seat each for women in the posts of vice-president, general secretary and joint general secretary. Pushpa Bhusal, Dila Sangroula (Pant) and Pratima Gautam were elected to those positions, respectively. Sangroula is the first woman to be elected general secretary in the party’s history.

The central committee elected at the Nepali Congress’s 15th general convention, held in Kathmandu from October 4 to 9, reflects broader representation across ethnic communities and professional groups. However, women remain below the one-third threshold among elected members, leaving the party president to meet the quota through his nominations.

For the central committee election, the party allocated a set number of seats for women across open and inclusion-based categories. Beyond the seats designated specifically for women, female members were elected through quotas for Khas Arya, Indigenous nationalities, Madhesi, Dalit, Tharu and Muslim communities. Women also secured places representing all seven provinces, Kathmandu Valley, under-35 youth, disadvantaged regions, overseas Nepali party committees, professional groups and workers.

The breakdown includes 15 women elected through the women’s open category, eight each from Indigenous nationalities and Khas Arya groups, and five each from Madhesi and Dalit communities. Tharu and Muslim groups elected two women each.

Two women were elected from professional groups and two through overseas Nepali party committees. Workers, the disadvantaged region category and Kathmandu Valley each accounted for one woman member. Seven women under 35 were elected through provincial youth representation, while another seven won seats in the province-based women’s open category.

Twelve women contested positions outside the reserved categories, but none was elected, underscoring the limits of women’s representation in seats not set aside for them.

Sangroula said women had secured a more substantial presence in the party leadership than in the past.

title: Former President Bhandari calls for trilateral cooperation in sharing meteorological data, monitoring glaciers - The Rising Nepal
description: Former President Bhandari calls for trilateral cooperation in sharing meteorological data, monitoring glaciers  The Rising Nepal

full_article:
By Mahendra Subedi, Xiong'an (China), Oct 24: Former President Bidya Devi Bhandari has called for stronger cooperation among Himalayan countries including Nepal, China and India in sharing meteorological data, monitoring glaciers, developing early warning systems and coordinating disaster response.

Addressing the 2026 Global Governance Forum in China’s Xiong’an city of Hebei Province earlier today, the former President said that global governance is also linked to climate justice and added that the unprecedented natural disasters Nepal experienced in August have underscored the gravity of the challenge. She noted that the Himalayas are a shared natural heritage connected to regional water cycles, biodiversity and ecological balance.

Likewise, she advocated strengthening the United Nations as an effective institution reflecting the diversity and aspirations of the contemporary world, adding that peace and development are mutually reinforcing. Ending poverty and hunger, promoting human well-being and redirecting resources from the arms race towards development are shared responsibilities, the former President added.

Delivering her speech in Nepali language, the former President expressed confidence that the Forum would foster meaningful deliberations towards making the global governance system more just, inclusive and effective, while creating new opportunities for cooperation for world peace, sustainable development and shared prosperity.

On Nepal-China relations, she noted that the bilateral ties have evolved since ancient times through cultural exchanges, Buddhist philosophy and close people-to-people links. She said the relationship is rooted in the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence and rests on mutual respect, trust and cooperation, reaffirming Nepal's unequivocal commitment to the One-China Policy.

Likewise, Bhandari said the world is undergoing rapid scientific and technological transformation while facing serious challenges including economic inequality, poverty, geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts, climate change and food insecurity. She was of the view that protectionism and unilateral approaches have complicated international cooperation, adding that such shared challenges cannot be resolved by any single nation and require dialogue and collective commitment.

The former president said that the international order founded on the UN Charter, international law and multilateralism has contributed significantly to peace and development, but reforms are needed to make it more inclusive, representative, transparent and effective.

"Global governance should not be shaped solely by the priorities of a limited number of nations," she said. "Differences among nations should be resolved through dialogue and diplomatic means," she added.

She further said the success of global governance should be measured by the positive changes it brings to people's lives.

The Forum was inaugurated by Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi on Friday evening.

Chinese President Xi Jinping’s message was also delivered to the 2026 Global Governance Forum. “The world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, and the deficits in peace, development, security and governance are growing rather than diminishing,” Xi stated.

The Global Governance Initiative (GGI) was forwarded to promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system and a better world, read the Chinese President’s message.

On the occasion, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang said all countries should uphold the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, keep development at the center of the international agenda, and fully implement the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

He also called for improving governance rules in emerging fields, turning new frontiers such as the deep sea, the polar regions and outer space into areas for international cooperation, and evolving an AI governance structure based on general consensus soon.

Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, the forum is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World."

Nearly 400 representatives from strategic, political, academic, business, media, and youth sectors from more than 90 countries and international and regional organizations, including the UN, attended the opening ceremony.(RSS)
